items.rootCause: This comes from tonight's B46 rework of Enter (Moving). Once a part was 'ended', React rendered [style, END] with no animated style, which took the animated style off the view (ViewDescriptorsSet.remove). 'Ended' could come from a JS safety timer at delay+1500 ms. When the UI thread stalls while it draws a screen's first frame (History's 8 cards, each with an SVG avatar), JS timers keep running and the UI-thread animation does not. So the safety timer took the style off while Reanimated's native AnimatedPropsRegistry still held what the UI thread last drew. That was the start (opacity 0, written when the style was put on) for cards 1-7, which were still inside their 40-280 ms stagger, and about half way for card 0. Nothing writes to that entry again once the style is off. Reanimated 4.5.1's settled-props sync (FORCE_REACT_RENDER_FOR_SETTLED_ANIMATIONS) then handed that stale value to JS. AnimatedComponent.render lays state.settledProps over the style and spreads them at the top of the props, for good (there is a 'TODO: revert when animated styles are detached'). That overrides React's END, so later commits (filter switches, scrolling) kept drawing the cards at alpha 0 / ~0.5. Before tonight the style stayed on, so the animation always ran out after the stall.
items.fix: Two changes in apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Enter.tsx (Moving). (1) Once a part has started, its animated style stays on the view until the part unmounts, so the UI thread always runs the entrance out and the registry's last value is the end. The safety timer no longer takes anything off. (2) The view is now AnimatedMovingView = Animated.createAnimatedComponent(MovingView). MovingView is a small function component that forwards ref to a View. Once the part is in (from the animation's end callbacks, or from the JS safety timer), it gets endStyle = END[kind] and lays it after everything Reanimated hands it, settled props included. It also drops the settled props Reanimated spreads at the top of the props (opacity/transform; Enter never passes those itself). So no sync, early or late, can hold a part anywhere but its end. Held parts are unchanged: their start is a plain React style and nothing animated is on them. Timings, kinds, stagger, springs and Reduced Motion (a plain View) are unchanged, so the visible animation is the same. This applies to every screen that uses Enter: Home, recent rows, History, Leaderboard, Progress, Modes/GameType/BotSelect, Splash/Login brand, the game board reveal, match views, friends room, connection overlays, ChapterUnlocked.
items.test: apps/mobile/src/components/ui/__tests__/enterSettled.test.tsx, test 'History: the UI thread stalls on its cards’ first frame; every card ends opaque and in place, after filters too'. The test now plays the native registry (registryOf: what the UI thread wrote while an animated style was on the view, kept unchanged once it comes off) and a stalled UI thread (stallUi/resumeUi: rAF frames held while JS timers run). Ten staggered rows; frames run 60 ms, then stall for 2.5 s; a settled sync runs during the stall; frames resume; filter switches follow. expectEnd checks three things: the host style is END, the registry is END, and there are no top-level opacity/transform props. On the old code it fails with card 0 at opacity 0.662 / translateY 4.05. Each half of the fix was disabled in turn to confirm it is needed: without END laid last, 6 tests fail; with the style taken off at the end, the registry checks fail.

items.rootCause: Same mechanism as E1, on Home's hero (kind 'settle', delay 120 ms, held until the Splash goes). Reanimated's withSpring advances at most 64 ms of spring time per frame (springOnFrame clamps deltaTime). On a cold start or after the language restart, the UI thread draws only a frame or two after the settle starts, then stalls while it draws Home's first frame. The JS safety timer (120+1500 ms) then took the animated style off. At that moment the registry held about 80 ms of spring, scale ≈0.966. That value was synced back as settledProps over React's scale 1, for good. The jest model of exactly this sequence gives scale 0.9665, matching the phone's box ([85..996] instead of [68..1013] = 0.964-0.968).
items.fix: Same fix as E1 (Enter.tsx). The settle spring now always runs to 1 on the UI thread, because the animated style is never taken off early. React's END {opacity 1, scale 1} is laid over any settled props once the part is in.

Frames resume and the end is dropped unsynced, then the account arrives. expectEnd('play', {opacity 1, scale 1}) runs first, then all parts. items.rootCause: B46's own restart case (RTL→RTL). After Updates.reloadAsync the UI thread is busy rebuilding the app just as the Splash goes and Home's parts start. Their animated styles were put on (the registry got the start, opacity 0), then the JS safety timers took them off before the UI thread ran their frames. The registry kept opacity 0, and the settled-props sync laid it over React's END for good. So the parts were drawn invisible but still took taps. A force-stop fixes it because the sync state lives in the component. Which parts stick depends on when the stall starts relative to each part's delay. The card (delay 0) could already be done, while the hero (120), 'again' (180) and recent header (220) were not, which matches the report.
items.fix: Same fix as E1 (Enter.tsx). The parts keep their animated styles until the UI thread has run them out, and once in, their END is laid over anything Reanimated syncs back. So no commit after the restart can draw them invisible.

enter.notes:
Checked against Reanimated 4.5.1 internals in node_modules:
- AnimatedComponent.render lays state.settledProps over the style and also spreads them at the top of the props. _syncStylePropsBackToReact only merges and is never reverted.
- ViewDescriptorsSet.remove leaves the AnimatedPropsRegistry entry as it is. getSettledUpdates returns entries 1-2 s old and drops older ones.
- ViewDescriptorsSet.add forces one write of the current values. springOnFrame clamps each frame to 64 ms, so a janky UI thread makes the spring lag behind JS time.
- PropsFilter only gives initial values to a style handle that was on the view at the first render.
- The jest model of the stall reproduces the phone's exact hero scale (0.9665).

Verification:
- I disabled each half of the fix in turn and the new tests failed each time, so both halves are needed.
- Tests run: Enter.test + enterSettled.test, plus every test folder of a screen using Enter (home, history, leaderboard, match, progress, friends, account, game/connection, boardReveal, ChapterUnlockedView) and startupGraph: 78 suites / 1091 tests passed.
- The game e2e tests (soloPractice, botPractice, ranked, historyReplay) passed: 4 suites / 20 tests.
- npx tsc -p apps/mobile --noEmit is clean. ESLint and prettier --check are clean on both changed files.

What I did not change:
- The global static feature flag.
- No locale strings and no docs: no doc describes this mechanism, and the visible motion is the same.
- No APK, adb, deploy or git commands were run.

By design (nothing to fix): 'parts that never start because their screen was blurred'.
- Only Home holds parts (play={enter}), and enter turns true whenever Home is shown and the Splash is gone. So a held part plays as soon as it can be seen; this is covered by homeEntrance.test 'waits for the Splash to go'.
- A part that starts while its screen is covered or in the background runs out when frames resume, and React's END is in place by then either way.

Remaining edge case, harmless: if the UI thread stalls for 2 s or more mid-animation and a commit lands meanwhile, one frame of END may show before the remaining frames. A part can no longer stay stuck.

For other owners, not changed (not my files):
- LevelResultView and StarRow (B11, levels-play) also keep the animated style on and add React {opacity: 1}. But that React value sits under Reanimated's settledProps, so a stale value synced during a UI stall could still stick there.
- The MovingView pattern in Enter.tsx (end laid after the settled props, top-level settled keys dropped) could be reused there.

issues.problem: The report says the fix covers 'match views, friends room, connection overlays, ChapterUnlocked'. None of these import ui/Enter. ChapterUnlockedView defines its own local Enter/Moving: an Animated.View whose animated style is always on, with no END laid after Reanimated's settledProps. So it keeps the latent weakness this round fixed in ui/Enter: a UI stall of 1 s or more mid-entrance syncs a stale value into settledProps, and if JS is then busy while the END entry is dropped, the stale value stays. LevelResultView and StarRow are in the same position; the agent did flag those two.
issues.evidence: grep `ui/Enter'` lists only Modes, GameType, Progress, Home, BotSelect, RecentGames, GameScreen (board and keypad reveal), History, Leaderboard, LoginArena, account/parts and SplashScreen. apps/mobile/src/screens/levels/ChapterUnlockedView.tsx:110-173 has `function Enter({reduce, kind, ...})` and `<Animated.View style={style}>` with useAnimatedStyle always attached. AnimatedComponent.tsx:538-544 lays state.settledProps after the user's style.
issues.suggestion: Correct the report's list of covered screens, so QA does not take ChapterUnlocked as fixed. Tell the levels owner they can reuse the MovingView pattern (END laid after settled props, top-level settled keys dropped), or move it to ui/Enter with new kinds.

issues.problem: A cosmetic edge case remains (it never sticks). If the UI thread is stalled from before a part's animated style is attached (restart or cold start) for longer than delay+1500 ms, the JS safety lays END while the registry has no entry yet. When the UI thread resumes, the queued forced write of the start and the animation may run after END was mounted. So one frame of the full END view can show, then the part drops to its start and plays the entrance. It still ends at END. The agent only noted the similar case 'stall 2 s or more mid-animation'.
issues.evidence: Enter.tsx:242: `setTimeout(() => setEnded(true), delayMs + ENTER.endSafetyMs)` is JS wall time. ViewDescriptorsSet.add and the `shown.set(withDelay(...))` from useEffect run on the UI runtime, which does not run while the UI thread is stalled. Adversarial test F (stall before mount) ends at END in the Jest model.
issues.suggestion: Nothing needed for E1-E3. If it shows up on a device, the safety could wait for a first UI-side signal (for example a worklet that marks the start) before laying END. Optional.

issues.problem: Older behaviour, not changed by this fix: a FlatList row with index below ENTER.cap that virtualization unmounts and mounts again (scroll far down and back) plays its rise again. Enter's header says a row 'a virtualized list mounts later as it scrolls appears at once', which holds only past the cap.
issues.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:215-225 and LeaderboardScreen.tsx:294-299 use `<Enter index={index}>` inside a FlatList renderItem. A remount creates a new Moving with started=play=true and a delay from staggerDelay(index).
issues.suggestion: No action for this regression. Optionally fix the wording of the header comment later.

review.summary:
I tried to refute the fix and could not: the root cause matches the Reanimated 4.5.1 source, and E1-E3 cannot recur in any scenario I could build. Only the three low-severity items above remain.

**Confirmed against the source**
- AnimatedComponent.render spreads state.settledProps at the top of the props and also appends them after the style (AnimatedComponent.tsx:538-544).
- _syncStylePropsBackToReact only merges.
- The native registry merges each view's updates (UpdatesRegistry.cpp:224-233). Its entries get timestamps on every write, are handed to JS when 1-2 s old, and are erased with no revert past 2 s (AnimatedPropsRegistry.cpp).

**Why it holds**
- With B46's [style, END] and the handle taken off at the end, a stale registry value synced back always outranks React's END. That is E1-E3.
- Now the handle stays on from start to unmount, so the UI thread always runs the entrance out and its last write is END. Timing and spring both finish exactly at toValue.
- `ended` is guaranteed: from the end callbacks, or the JS safety at delay+1500 ms, which is re-armed if the effect runs again.
- Once ended, MovingView lays END after everything Reanimated passes, settled props included, and drops the top-level opacity/transform. Enter never sets those itself.
- So whatever the registry did (dropped unsynced, stale sync, a React commit after the drop), React's own props end at END.

**Wiring checked**
- createAnimatedComponent(MovingView) works: React 19 passes ref as a prop to the View, so findHostInstance takes its fast path.
- collapsable=false and nativeID reach the View, endStyle passes through PropsFilter, and the CSSManager falls back to stylePropsBuilder.

**Home's held parts can't get stuck**
- Only Home holds parts.
- useAuthGate shows the Splash whenever status is 'loading', so Home visible means splashGone.
- A part that mounts after Home is blurred mounts as a plain View (entrance false).

**Visible animation**
- The same as before tonight: same kinds, timings, easing, springs and stagger.
- A part that plays at mount still gets the handle's initial values on its first render.
- A held part keeps START under a late-attached handle.
- Reduced Motion is still a plain View.
- END only matches values the UI has already reached, so it causes no flash in normal conditions.

**Tests I ran**
- The current suites pass: enterSettled, Enter and homeEntrance (21 tests); the home, history, leaderboard, progress, account and ui folders (64 suites, 904 tests). tsc is clean; eslint and prettier --check are clean on both changed files.
- I rebuilt the B46 Enter (Animated.View, `!started ? [style,start] : ended ? [style,END] : [style,start,animated]`) and ran it through a moduleNameMapper. The 3 new tests fail on it with the values in the report: scale 0.9665 / opacity 0.86, opacity 0 / translateY 12, and opacity 0.662 / translateY 4.05.
- On the pre-tonight version (af4c8a5), 4 of the 5 tests in the file fail.
- I wrote 7 adversarial tests:
  - a 1.1 s stall with a stale sync before the safety;
  - a filter switch during the stall (indices change mid-entrance), then 'All' again under a second stall;
  - 4 s in the background mid-pop;
  - the UI stalled from before mount;
  - an index shift after a synced END, then a stall;
  - play true then false at once (Home blurred);
  - unmount mid-stall.
- All 7 pass on the current code. 6 of them fail on the B46 rebuild.
- Two partial variants fail too:
  - keeping the handle on without laying END: 9 of 12 fail;
  - laying END but taking the handle off at the end: 7 of 12 fail.
  So both halves of the fix are needed.

**Limits**
- The tests model the native registry and the settled sync in Jest. Only the device checks in the report confirm the real thing.
- The FlatList cases are modelled with plain rows. FlatList does not recycle cells, and keys are by game id.
- Reduced Motion, fast navigation away and back, and unmount mid-animation are all safe by construction.

I did not edit any repo files. My scratch files are under C:/Users/mosheg/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/c--Users-mosheg-Documents-ReactNative-sudoku-fight/4440d2fa-e446-41ad-83db-f79035cdf42c/scratchpad/rev-e/ (b46/Enter.tsx, tests/adv.test.tsx, jest.adv.config.js, jest.variant.config.js).

items.rootCause:
The replay draws PlayerCardCompact for every player. That card has fixed rows: score 24 dp, activity 16 dp, card 160 dp.
(1) Score: it is a TextInput (CountUpText). Its natural box is paddingTop 4 + a 25 line = 29 dp. Inside a fixed 24 dp row, Yoga measures it AT_MOST 24 and RN clamps the box (TextLayoutManager.calculateHeight). An EditText shorter than its line scrolls to its last line, so the tops of the digits are drawn off its top edge. This already shows at normal size: the 1.0 screenshot draws '0' as a 'U'. At ×1.35 it is worse ('4.5' loses its top half).
(2) The activity words ('חושב', the cell, the blinking ellipsis), the rating, the place badge '#2', the hit chip, the reconnect pill and the ring's seconds had no font-scale cap. At ×2.0 they outgrew their fixed rows and badges.
(3) The flag (13 px emoji) was uncapped and sits on the 34 dp avatar, so at ×2.0 it covered most of it. The uncapped '#2' badge plus the ×1.35 bot chip covered Pip's avatar.
(4) ScreenHeader drew the subtitle with numberOfLines 1, so it ended in '…'. The title 'צפייה חוזרת' (292 dp at ×2 in about 229 dp) would also be cut.
items.fix:
PlayerCardCompact: new compactRows(fontScale). Every word on the card now grows up to the HUD cap (×1.35), and the rows grow with it: score row round(24·s), activity row a least height of round(16·s). The score TextInput gets negative vertical margins, -(box-row)/2 - 1, so Yoga gives it its whole box centred on the row. The row keeps its designed height, so nothing moves at 1.0.
Card: minHeight 160 instead of a fixed height. It reserves the 36 dp strip only when the strip shows something. In the replay (no buttons) cards stay 160 even at the cap. A ranked 3–4 player card in a game may grow about 23 dp at the largest sizes instead of overlapping its buttons.
Caps: scale 'hud' on ActivityLine compact (word, cell, ellipsis), Rating (new `scale` prop), RankBadge, HitChip and ReconnectPill. Scale 'board' (×1.0) on the TimerRing seconds (fixed ring), on Flag (new `scale` prop) and on the bot chip (new Avatar `botScale` prop) on the compact card's avatar. The DeltaLabel float now sits at bottom '100%'.
ScreenHeader: new opt-in `wrapSubtitle` (adds testID screen-subtitle). The replay header now uses wrapTitle + wrapSubtitle: two whole lines, never '…'.
docs/design/components.md §2 (bot chip) and §7.2 (new 'Text size' row) are updated.

items.rootCause:
ExplanationCard joined its label parts with spaceSentences (match:sentenceSpace), which assumes every part already ends as a sentence. Two kinds of part don't:
- 'explain.played' ('5ではなく1' / '1 במקום 5');
- the 'label: value' calculation lines (and 'noLogic').
Japanese and Chinese have an empty sentenceSpace, so '5ではなく1' ran straight into '1が入らない理由…' ('…5ではなく11が…'). In other languages the parts were only separated by a space, with no stop and no pause.
items.fix: compose.ts gains endsSentence() (the last mark is . ! ? … 。 ！ ？ ؟ ।, ignoring trailing isolates and ZWSP) and closeSentences(parts, t). closeSentences closes each part that isn't a sentence yet with common:text.sentence (the language's own full stop: '.', '。', none in Thai), then spaces them with match:sentenceSpace. ExplanationCard uses closeSentences, so every language gets a separator. Example: '…5ではなく1。1が入らない理由：…。得点：…。' and in Hebrew '…1 במקום 5. למה 1 לא מתאים: …'.

So 'งก์' dropped to a second line that the one-line label never shows, leaving 'แร'.

items.rootCause:
This is general, not Arabic-specific. RN 0.86 measures every Text for Yoga in TextLayoutManager with a StaticLayout that breaks lines by glyph advances (Builder default). It sizes the view to that: AT_MOST width is min(desiredWidth, floor(width)), and the height is the measured layout's line count. RN has an unused setUseBoundsForWidth reflection field there.
The view that draws the text is a TextView (ReactTextView; ReactEditText for TextInput), which lays the text out again. Since Android 15, TextView.useBoundsForWidth is 'true by default if the target API version is 35 or later'. The app targets 36, and the A16 runs Android 16. So at draw time lines break by glyph bounding boxes.
A glyph whose ink reaches past its advance makes the drawn line 1–2 px wider than the measured box: Rubik's isolated ر and ز have xMin −49/1000 em (measured from the font file), and final forms such as ع have tails. The last word wraps onto a line the box has no height for, so it is hidden with no '…'. This matches the reports:
- 'سلسلة الفوز' (ends in an isolated ز) measured as one line in its 175 px tile;
- 'تدريب فردي · سريع' measured as exactly 289 px, with free space beside it.
Rubik's Hebrew and Latin glyphs are inside their advances (only 'j' overhangs; Teko has none), which is why Hebrew was not affected.
items.fix:
New config plugin apps/mobile/plugins/withTextAdvanceWidths.js, registered in apps/mobile/app.json (app.config.ts was not touched). It adds <item name="android:useBoundsForWidth" tools:targetApi="35">false</item> to AppTheme in styles.xml. Every TextView and EditText then breaks lines by advances, the same model RN measures with, as on Android ≤14. The attribute is public since API 35 (0x1010698, in the android-35/36 R). Older Android ignores it, and iOS is untouched.
I checked the full Android mod pipeline (getPrebuildConfigAsync + compileModsAsync, introspect, android only): AppTheme ends with ['android:useBoundsForWidth','false','35'].
Needs a native rebuild. `npm run apk` re-prebuilds automatically because app.json changed and appJsonFiles hashes the plugin file.

text.notes:
1. T5 and T6 are native changes (a theme item from a config plugin). They reach the phone only with a new APK built through prebuild. `npm run apk` does this automatically because app.json changed. An OTA/JS-only update will not fix them. I did not touch app.config.ts, build-apk.*, the BUILD-APK docs or any other peer file. The plugin goes through app.json, which appJsonFiles hashes.

2. The default I relied on comes from the platform docs for TextView.setUseBoundsForWidth ('true by default if the target API version is 35 or later'; the app's targetSdk is 36, in node_modules/react-native/gradle/libs.versions.toml). Sources: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/android.widget.textview.useboundsforwidth?view=net-android-36.0 (mirrors the AOSP Javadoc) and https://developer.android.com/reference/android/widget/TextView#setUseBoundsForWidth(boolean). Also https://developer.android.com/about/versions/16/behavior-changes-16 for the elegantTextHeight change.

3. Residual risk for T5: Thai uses the system font. On Android 15+ both RN's measuring TextPaint and the TextView use the elegant (non-UI) font variant: the Paint default follows deprecate_ui_fonts, and Android 16 ignores elegantTextHeight for target 36. So the bounds mismatch is the expected cause, but this is unverified on the phone. If 'แร' persists on the new APK, the next suspect is a font-variant mismatch, and the safe minimum would be letting short chip labels stretch to the chip's width.

4. Side effect of the general T6 fix (pre-Android-15 behaviour, accepted): a glyph whose ink passes its advance at the very edge of its Text can be shaved by up to about 1–2 px. Measured in the font files: Rubik's isolated ر and ز (about 0.6 dp at 12 px), and Latin 'j'. Teko and Hebrew have none.

5. T1 at the right level means PlayerCardCompact changed for the in-game 3–4 player HUD too:
- At font_scale 1.0 the in-game card is unchanged (minHeight 160 = content 123 + strip 36). The score's digit tops, which were also clipped at 1.0 (the '0' drawn as a 'U'), are now whole.
- In Arabic or Thai at 1.0, a ranked card with a rating may grow 1–4 dp, where its content used to overlap the strip.
- At the largest sizes a ranked 3–4 player card grows about 23 dp, and GameScreen's board fits the remaining room.
- geometry.ts compactScoreSlotOf and reactions/model.ts still assume fixed rows and 160 dp, so at large text the score chip's landing point and the reaction origin can be a few dp off. Not changed: cosmetic, and not in my items.

6. Decisions that may be Moshe's:
- The replay header now wraps its title and subtitle to two lines at large text. I picked that over shrinking the title to 70%.
- On the compact card's avatar the flag and the bot chip stay at design size (×1.0). Elsewhere the bot chip keeps ×1.35; results tests still require that.
- The replay card's screen-reader label now has a full stop after '1 במקום 5' and after the calculation lines in Hebrew and English too.

7. Golden explanations: explainGolden.json is the engine's old wording and must never be regenerated. The test now maps the app's Hebrew 'בה' back to 'בו' in row/column hidden-single sentences only, documented as a deliberate correction. The rest of the corpus still matches word for word.

- Jest: player components, replay, game (incl. GroupHud), home, results, history, player card, levels, i18n, components/ui, e2e historyReplay/ranked/solo/bot. All pass, except components/ui/__tests__/tactile.test.tsx, which failed once in a parallel run but passes alone. It is not related to my changes.
